text:
Nathan MacKinnon has 30 points in 18 games, and the unsettling part for the rest of the league is how little of it looks like a fluke. He's skating 20.7 minutes a night, his top speed sits at the very top of the league's tracking, and our style comparisons match him most closely with Nikita Kucherov: a setup man whose team creates a lot with him on. Coming off a Rocket Richard Trophy, he's drawing "on pace for historic" headlines.

The one place to tap the brakes is the finishing. His 10 goals came on 7.1 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and a 15% shooting rate rarely lasts 82 games. Our projection still lands around 122 points, with a range of 107 to 138.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 3.7 wins last season, fifth among forwards, almost all from even-strength offense. The week's other storyline came from off the ice: NDTV Sports and Heavy.com both reported unexpected criticism from former Avalanche teammate Erik Johnson. MacKinnon answered on the ice, in on three goals in Saturday's 4-0 win over Detroit.
headline: MacKinnon is running hot, and mostly earning it
